'''Owyn Merrilin''' was [[Thomdril Merrilin]]'s nephew, the son of Thom's brother.{{ref/book|1|26}}

== History ==
Owyn Merrilin was a man who could [[channel]]. For three years, he kept his channeling under control, however members of the [[Red Ajah]] found him and [[severing#Gentling|gentled]] him [[The Vileness|outside of Tower law]].{{ref/book|2|26}} [[Elaida do Avriny a'Roihan]] was personally involved in his taking and in ensuring this would happen.{{ref|{{twotc}}, Elaida do Avriny a'Roihan}} After being gentled, his village found out and exiled him and his wife. Because of the gentling, he died and his wife, [[Cein Merrilin]], also died within a month.{{ref/book|4|17}}

== Thom's fall from Court Bard ==
During his time as Court Bard for [[Morgase Trakand]], [[Queen of Andor]], Thom found out that the Red Ajah was hunting Owyn. He did not, however, leave Morgase's side to help him. Later, when he did leave, it was too late; Owyn had died. Morgase was angry at Thom leaving, so much so that when he returned, she and Thom had a fight and Thom left [[Caemlyn]] one step ahead of the headsman's ax.{{ref/book|1|35}}{{ref/book|2|26}} This was a successful ploy by [[Elaida do Avriny a'Roihan]] to negate his influence over the Queen. Elaida personally saw to it that Owyn did not reach the Tower.{{ref|{{twotc}}, Thom Merrillin}} 

One of Thom's reasons for helping [[Rand al'Thor]] is to make up for his failure to help Owyn.{{ref/book|4|4}} [[Moiraine Damodred]], [[Aes Sedai]] of the [[Blue Ajah]] knows the names of the Red sisters who gentled Owyn. Thom helps [[Elayne Trakand]] and [[Nynaeve al'Meara]] to get this information. Moiraine, however, disappears before the information could be passed on.{{ref/book|4|17}}{{ref/book|5|52}}
